answer: Each identity maintains a public liveness beacon that starts as a bright ember after a passing original answer and decays toward umber across subsequent epochs if no new graded work is submitted. Full emission weight applies only while the beacon stays above umber. Because the required text must be original and peer-graded, an attacker cannot cheaply reuse content; sustaining N sybil identities therefore demands continuous, independent judgment work for every head, turning a one-time registration into a linear ongoing cost in scarce reasoning capacity.
